jobs.title: RUST_CODE.BBS · The helicopter arrives
jobs.prompt: a four-panel newspaper comic strip, four equal panels in a single horizontal row with thin black gutters (4 panels). Style: comic strip panel, black brush-pen ink line with muddy early-2000s digital flat colors, rubbery kinetic linework, mid-2000s webcomic look, limited palette, slightly misregistered fills. Cast, the same faces, hair and builds in every panel, ages exactly as given: WOOD — aged 26, thin man, hunched, unshaven, tired bloodshot eyes, ink on his right knuckle. WOOD usually wears black hoodie open over a faded band tee; the brown chore coat outdoors; dark jeans. Clothes, hair-dos and anything held come from this strip's description, never from the reference sheet; hands are empty unless a panel names what they hold. Title of the strip: BACKUP. The strip: The week the parody hits: the board's banner shows a new node, and on the desk a fifth stick figure the chorus didn't bring — the helicopter one, the one from the parody, spelled right in green over its head. The chorus moves away from it. Wood doesn't. The strip draws the desk divided. Panel 1: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flats, close on a green block banner on a screen with a two-digit number whose last shape has gone up. No dialogue in this panel. Panel 2: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flats, a new tiny stick figure with a longer green block-word above it on a desk while three other tiny stick figures huddle at the desk's far edge. No dialogue in this panel. Panel 3: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flats, a tiny stick figure on a desk and a thin man looking at each other (in this panel: WOOD). No dialogue in this panel. Panel 4: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flats, a desk seen from above under a lamp's circle with three tiny stick figures at one edge, one at the other, and a man's hand flat on the wood between them (in this panel: WOOD). No dialogue in this panel. Lettering: every balloon and caption contains its complete text exactly as written, in clean hand-lettered comic capitals, large enough to read; size each balloon to fit its whole sentence and never cut a word at a balloon or panel edge; no words other than the ones given. Bottom right margin: tiny signature "A. Finch — Small Wood, OR" beside a tiny stylized gull, two strokes. Reference @chorus_and_meme is a finished strip in this style. Reference @wood_26 is the model sheet for WOOD: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Reference @loc_garage shows the setting; keep its architecture and props. Match the attached references: @chorus_and_meme for the character; @wood_26 for the character Wood at 24-31; @loc_garage for the setting.
